title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Scheduling Operations Agent optimises multiple resources at once
summary: The briefing largely matches the roadmap and Microsoft's preview documentation, including the differing batch limits and the documented controls. However, its default-state field describes initial agent setup rather than this expansion, which Microsoft says arrives automatically for organizations already using the agent.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans multi-resource schedule optimization in Dynamics 365 Field Service's Scheduling Operations Agent.
claims.quote: This release expands the optimization capabilities of the Scheduling Operations Agent to include multiple resources.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists optimization of up to five resources directly from the schedule board.
claims.quote: Optimize schedules for up to 5 resources directly from the schedule board.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists optimization of up to 30 resources using an optimization plan.
claims.quote: Optimize schedules for up to 30 resources using an optimization plan.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists custom goals and weighted objectives.
claims.quote: Create custom goals and weight objectives.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists custom optimization scopes for plans.
claims.quote: Create custom optimization scopes to use with your optimization plans.

claims.claim: Dispatchers can compare proposed and current schedules before applying changes.
claims.quote: Dispatchers can review and compare the proposed schedules with the current schedules before applying changes.

claims.claim: The expansion builds on an existing public preview.
claims.quote: These capabilities build on the existing public preview of the Scheduling Operations Agent

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Interactive optimization supports up to five resources.
claims.quote: Up to 5. A resource with a capacity greater than 1 counts as one resource for each capacity point.
claims.fix: After the interactive five-resource limit, add: 'A resource with capacity greater than 1 counts once per capacity point.' Apply the same qualification to the governance reminder; the limits page states this qualification.

claims.claim: Interactive optimization supports up to 120 jobs.
claims.quote: Each interactive optimization supports up to five selected resources, up to 120 jobs (existing bookings and open requirements combined)

claims.claim: Interactive optimization supports a window of up to 72 hours.
claims.quote: an optimization window of up to 72 hours.

claims.claim: Batch optimization runs asynchronously.
claims.quote: The optimization runs asynchronously, so you can continue working while the agent processes the request.

claims.claim: A plan combines a scope, goal and time range.
claims.quote: A plan combines a scope, a goal, and a time range.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A scope defines the resources, open requirements and existing bookings a batch run considers.
claims.quote: A scope defines the set of data that a batch optimization operates over - which resources to optimize, which unfulfilled requirements to consider, and which existing bookings the agent can change.

claims.claim: Plans can run on demand or on a recurring schedule.
claims.quote: Run a plan on demand or on a recurring schedule.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The minimum plan recurrence interval is 30 minutes.
claims.quote: The minimum interval is 30 minutes.

claims.claim: Apply automatically applies batch results as soon as optimization finishes, without a prior review step.
claims.quote: Apply automatically applies the results as soon as the optimization finishes.

claims.claim: Each included custom-goal objective receives a weight from 1 to 10.
claims.quote: In a custom goal, select which objectives to include and assign each one a weight from 1 to 10.

claims.quote: | Optimization range | Up to 14 days. |

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits consumed by an optimization request depend on its resource count, with more resources using more capacity.
claims.quote: a single optimization request consumes credits based on the number of resources it includes, so optimizing more resources at once uses more capacity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[2].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent can move or delete bookings whose status has Optimization Method set to Optimize.
claims.quote: Optimize: The agent can move or delete bookings with this status to generate an optimal schedule.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Rollout; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Initial use of the agent requires administrator setup and enabling its toggle.
claims.quote: Before dispatchers can use the agent, an administrator must set it up in your environment.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: One agent toggle enables both interactive and batch optimizations.
claims.quote: Turning on the agent enables both interactive and batch optimizations.

claims.claim: The expansion does not turn the agent on for organizations that have not enabled it.
claims.quote: will be automatically enabled for all organizations that have the agent enabled.

claims.claim: No separate switch is documented for the multi-resource, goal, scope and plan expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent multi-resource enable switch. Read soa-setup, soa-overview, soa-interactive-optimizations, soa-goals, soa-scopes and soa-plans; they document the shared agent toggle, not a separate expansion switch.

claims.claim: Scopes store fetchXML queries rather than references to the original views.
claims.quote: A scope stores the fetchXML query that's evaluated when the optimization runs, not a reference to the view used.

claims.claim: The agent truncates scope query results that exceed supported record counts.
claims.quote: If a query returns more records than the optimization supports, the agent truncates the list.

claims.claim: The agent runs as an application user belonging to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: The agent runs as an application user that belongs to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.

claims.claim: The agent's application user has default read and write access to standard scheduling tables.
claims.quote: By default, the agent's application user can read and write the standard scheduling tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Assigning matching team security roles grants the agent access to custom tables used by optimizations.
claims.quote: assign the matching security roles to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team so that the agent can read and update those tables.

claims.claim: Changes use the combined permissions of the initiating user and application user, both of which need record access.
claims.quote: Each change the agent makes uses the combined permissions of the user who runs the optimization and the agent's application user, so both must have access to the affected records.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator grants creation of scopes, goals and plans.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator | Administrators who create scopes, goals, and plans | Create, edit, and delete scopes, goals, and plans, and view optimization results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Scheduling Operations Agent User grants running interactive optimizations and existing batch plans.
claims.quote: View scopes, goals, and plans; run interactive optimizations from the schedule board and batch optimizations from a plan; and view optimization results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The team must be added to field security profiles covering columns referenced by scopes or queries.
claims.quote: If you use column-level security (field security profiles) on any columns that your scopes or queries reference, also add the Scheduling Operations Agent Team to the matching field security profile.

claims.claim: Without matching field security profile access, the agent may ignore column filters and produce incorrect results.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the agent might ignore filter conditions on those columns and return incorrect results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[2].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An unset booking status Optimization Method is treated as Do Not Move.
claims.quote: If you don't set this field, the agent treats all bookings in that status as Do Not Move.

claims.claim: Batch requests cannot be applied after 72 hours or after their time range starts.
claims.quote: You can't apply a request that's more than 72 hours old or past the start of its time range.

claims.claim: With Always match time window selected, an expired promise window causes the booking's deletion from the suggested schedule.
claims.quote: If you select this option and a booking in the optimization range has an expired promise window, the agent deletes that booking from the suggested schedule.

claims.claim: When resource or job limits are exceeded, some records are dropped.
claims.quote: When an optimization has more resources or jobs than the limit allows, the agent keeps the most relevant records and drops the rest.

claims.claim: Optimization fails when existing bookings alone exceed the job limit.
claims.quote: If the existing bookings alone exceed the jobs limit, the optimization fails.

claims.claim: Equipment, Pool and Facility resource types are unsupported.
claims.quote: It doesn't support resources of type Equipment, Pool, and Facility.

claims.claim: Requirement groups and multiday requirements are unsupported.
claims.quote: It doesn't support requirement groups or multiday requirements (requirements that are related to requirement detail records).

claims.claim: Four or more breaks per work day or shift cause a resource error.
claims.quote: A resource can have up to three breaks per work day or shift. With four or more breaks, the agent returns an error.

For each booking status, set the Optimization Method property

Update: PATCH /msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplans(msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplanid)
LogicalName | msdyn_applymethod

claims.claim: The default state of this multi-resource expansion is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: These capabilities build on the existing public preview of the Scheduling Operations Agent and will be automatically enabled for all organizations that have the agent enabled.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'on' for this expansion. Retain the existing qualification that automatic enablement applies to organizations that already have the agent enabled, and that initial agent setup still requires an administrator.

claims.claim: The action rating is review although the expansion arrives automatically for existing agent organizations.
claims.quote:
action: "review"
The roadmap says the new capabilities are enabled automatically for organisations that have the agent enabled.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': the expansion arrives automatically for existing agent organizations, has metered usage and scheduling controls to review, and its March CY2027 target is more than 60 days after the run date.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to configure or review has a controls-table row.
claims.quote:
Confirm a billing model is in place
Give the Scheduling Operations Agent Team the roles it needs
add it to field security profiles
Audit recurring plans for their Apply method and recurrence interval
claims.fix: The checklist steps to configure billing capacity, grant agent-team security roles, add the team to field security profiles and audit recurrence intervals have no corresponding controls-table rows. Keep these as background rather than checklist instructions; no new rows are requested.

claims.claim: The Field Service BookingStatus extension documents writable msdyn_optimizationmethod and its Optimize, Do Not Move and Ignore values.
claims.quote:
Writable columns/attributes: msdyn_OptimizationMethod
LogicalName | msdyn_optimizationmethod
192350000 | Optimize
192350001 | Do Not Move
192350002 | Ignore

claims.claim: The agent team's security roles are assigned through Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Teams > Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote:
In the Power Platform admin center, select your environment, and then go to Settings > Teams.
Select the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
Assign the security roles that grant access to the tables your optimizations use, and then save.
